My fiancé would like to get me a new mechanical for my office for my birthday. This is fantastic news! But normally I like blue switches and I hear that those are not the best for the office environment. (clack) So, I humbly ask you, fellow keyboard enthusiasts, would you ever so kindly link me to what you think is the best board for office use?

Cherry Browns or Clears are the closed to the feeling of Blue switches but without that 'click', you could add O-Rings if the keyboard is still to loud. Browns feel a little less tactile, clears feel a little more tactile than blues. Both are brilliant switches to use.

What size keyboard are you looking for; full size, tenkeyless, 60% or a special size? And what's your budget?

As for recommendations, this is the one I'd choose. Its not crazy looking, it's built like a tank and it feels so fantastic!

I am trying to keep it within $130

Size is not all that important, a 10 keyless is what I usually like.

To be honest, any keyboard around $120 would be a great board. The CM Quickfire Rapid is a very decent board, my friend has one and it's great. Any from the KUL range are very good too, you're paying a little more for better quality parts.

Most keyboards around that price range come with backlighting or extra "gamer stuff" which you probably dont want for work.
What do you think of Das Keyboards?

Das Keyboard Ultimates are really good, 3 and 4 are high quality boards with no bad features. The Ultimate 4C has had some bad reviews though (its the mini version of the Das Ultimate 4) as it has non-cherry switches. Top quality boards for a decent price imo. :)
I am using a Poseidon Z at the moment and it is pretty nice. My friend got a Das for work and he has loved it. Not sure if I will miss the heavier bump of the blues though.
A word about Das keyboards: The new Das boards (4, 4c, etc) are no longer manufactured by Costar. The quality has dropped from their Costar days, as they are now made in China. OEM unknown.

MX Brown switches and the Filco if you can afford it or the CM if not. Also, a used Filco from a member of either DeskThority or GeekHack might also fit the bill. I wouldn't buy a used CM, but the Filcos are very well built. (Okay, I have bought a used CM, but I wouldn't recommend you do so for your work keyboard.)

Especially for work, avoid the flashy keyboards where you are paying extra for glitz instead of quality.
I got this and added O-rings. I don't get any complaints about sound once I added the O-rings. Here is the smaller version

I am using a Steel Series G6V2 with red switches and O-rings at work, not the same feeling as my other keyboards I normally use (Blues) but still a nice experience. You can normally get it on sale around $100 in Canada, but I do some number crunching so I needed the numpad.

You could also look into a Topre board. The Topre Type Heaven goes for $130 on eBay. I recently got a Topre board and I'm converted. It's quieter than any MX switch I've used, and the smooth actuation is amazing. Lovely "thock"!
